---
title: "Configuration"
---

Environment variables control how `jupyter-positron-server` runs Positron Server
inside your Jupyter environment.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE` | Path to a license file that `jupyter-positron-server` passes to `positron-server` as `--license-key-file`. On Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer, this file can be a raw `license.lic`. Leave it unset when the license file sits in the activation directory at `<positron-server-path>/resources/activation/linux/<arch>/license.lic`, which is where `positron-server` looks by default. |
| `POSITRON_LICENSE_MINTING_ENDPOINT` | URL of the JupyterHub minting endpoint that issues short-lived signed license tokens. Applies to Positron Server 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2 only. Takes precedence over `POSITRON_LICENSE_KEY_FILE`. See [Verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd). |
| `POSITRON_CONNECTION_TOKEN` | Sets the connection token that Positron Server validates on every request. Defaults to a random token for each session. Set it per session from a `pre_spawn_hook` to land students in Positron Server through `Spawner.default_url`. Do not set one fixed value for all sessions. See [Common settings](common_settings.qmd#start-students-in-positron-server). |
| `POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` | JSON object of Positron settings that students cannot change. See [Admin-enforced settings](#admin-enforced-settings). |
| `POSITRON_HOST` | Host address for Positron Server to bind to. Defaults to `127.0.0.1`. |
| `JSP_DEFAULT_FOLDER` | Directory that Positron Server opens. Defaults to `JUPYTERHUB_ROOT_DIR`, then `HOME`. |
| `JSP_POSITRON_LAUNCHER_DISABLED` | Set to any value to hide the Positron tile in the JupyterLab launcher. |

::: callout-note
On Positron Server 2026.09.0 and newer, a license needs no environment variable
at all. `positron-server` finds `license.lic` in its own activation directory.
Both license variables are for deployments that keep the file somewhere else, or
that still run on 2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2.
:::

## Admin-enforced settings

`POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` lets administrators lock Positron settings so
students cannot override them through the Settings UI, or by editing
`settings.json` directly. Locked settings appear grayed out with a policy
indicator. Enforced settings survive profile changes, workspace switches, and
direct edits to `~/.positron-server/data/User/settings.json`.

**Requirements**: `jupyter-positron-server` 0.0.4 or newer, and Positron Server
2026.07.1-5 or newer.

Create the config file:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
cat > /opt/tljh/config/jupyterhub_config.d/positron_enforced.py << 'EOF'
c.SystemdSpawner.environment.update({
    'POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS': '{"workbench.colorTheme":"Default Positron Dark","extensions.autoUpdate":false}'
})
EOF
```

Sessions that are already running keep their settings until a student starts a
new session.

::: callout-important
The TLJH install script sets `PATH` in `c.SystemdSpawner.environment`. A setting on
the spawner class takes precedence over `c.Spawner`, so on TLJH, JupyterHub ignores
`c.Spawner.environment`. Use `.update()` to add to the dictionary, because an
assignment replaces it. The file name `positron_enforced.py` sorts after
`positron.py`, so the update runs after the install script's assignment.
:::

## Memory requirements

Allocate at least 2.5 GB of RAM per Positron Server session. The right amount
depends on the size of the workload:

- **Light**: single console, few extensions, simple scripts, basic app development
- **Standard**: runtime switching, multiple consoles, multiple extensions, app development
- **Heavy**: memory-intensive extensions such as file watchers or language servers, multiple concurrent apps, large datasets

Use the table below to match each workload level to its minimum and recommended
memory allocation.

| Workload | Minimum | Recommended |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| Light | 2 GB | 2.5 GB |
| Standard | 2.5 GB | 4 GB |
| Heavy | 4 GB | 6 GB or more |

Signs of insufficient memory include slow runtime switching, extensions that fail
to install, degraded app performance, and crashes during memory-intensive
operations.

::: callout-note
For the full guidance this section summarizes, see the Positron Pro
[memory allocation FAQ](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/user/positron/reference/faq.html#allocate-sufficient-memory-for-your-positron-pro-session).
:::

## Hub license minting

::: callout-note
Hub license minting is a former way of working, scoped to Positron Server
2026.07.0 through 2026.08.2, and not recommended for a new deployment. Positron
Server 2026.09.0 and newer validate `license.lic` directly and need no minting
service. See [Verifier setup](verifier_get_started.qmd) only if you are
deploying that exact version range.
:::
